The failing test `testHeaderMissingWithNull()` is testing a scenario where the CSV header is missing with a nullString set to "". The test creates a `CSVFormat` with a header, sets a nullString to "", and parses a CSV input.

Based on the current bug report, a NullPointerException is thrown when setting the format to have a nullString of "" and having an empty header value.

Looking at the `CSVFormat` class, it seems that the `CSVFormat` constructor method allows for setting various parameters including the `header`, `nullString`, `skipHeaderRecord`, and `ignoreEmptyHeaders`.

Unfortunately, I couldn't retrieve the specific code snippet related to the `withHeader().withNullString().parse()` chain, but based on the description provided and the behavior observed, the issue is likely caused by a missing check or handling for the case when the header is empty and the nullString is set to "".

To diagnose the issue further, I would suggest inspecting the implementation of the methods `withHeader()`, `withNullString()`, and `parse()` in the `CSVFormat` class to identify any potential nullPointerExceptions or improper handling of empty headers with nullStrings set to "".

Possible fix:
- `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.withHeader(char[], java.lang.String, boolean).withNullString(java.lang.String).parse(java.io.Reader)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
